subject: Penetration test report sharing / NDA & redaction negotiation
messages:
From: J. Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme-corp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pen-test report request and NDA for redactions

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our security review ahead of the procurement committee next month, our InfoSec team has asked for a copy of Redwood's most recent penetration test executive summary and, if possible, the full report under an NDA. Our legal team flagged redactions will be required for any detailed findings that could disclose internal mitigations or exploit proof-of-concept.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will share an exec summary now?
- What your redaction policy is for full reports and whether you’ll provide a redaction log?
- Any timing constraints — ideally we’d like to review material before 03/01.

I can loop in our legal counsel if needed.

Best,
Jon Sullivan\InfoSec Manager\Acme Analytics

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen-test report request and NDA for redactions

Hi Jon —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: we can share an executive summary under a mutual NDA quickly; a full pen-test report can be shared but requires an internal redaction review and a redaction log, and typically takes a few business days after NDA execution.

For context on policy: we do not share raw exploit code or PII. Our usual process is:
- Sign mutual NDA (we can provide a template)
- Redwood security performs redaction pass, produces a redaction log (high-level categories redacted)
- Share exec summary immediately (often unredacted), sanitized/full report after approval

Attaching our NDA template and a short note on redaction levels. Rafael (security) and Karthik (sales/legal ops) are copied to coordinate.

Would you prefer DocuSign or your counsel edits?

Best,
Laura Bennett\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: NDA-redaction-request.docx (docx stub)

From: Ellie Conway <ellie.conway@redbridge-legal.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, J. Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pen-test report request and NDA for redactions

Laura/Jon —

Thanks. A couple quick points from Acme legal:
1) We prefer to propose markups on your mutual NDA instead of a fresh DocuSign signature, to ensure our standard liability and retention clauses are present.
2) For the pen test, we would like the executive summary plus a "sanitized" findings section that preserves severity and vectors but removes exploit PoC. We will not accept a report with entire categories redacted (e.g., all web app findings) — we need enough detail to evaluate remediation risk.

Can your security team confirm what level of granularity you can provide and share an estimated timeline once NDA markups are received?

Regards,
Ellie Conway\Senior Counsel\Redbridge Legal (on behalf of Acme)

---
Attachment: acme_nda_markups.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: redaction approach & remediation status for Acme request

Laura/Karthik —

Quick security note to support the external thread. Recommended approach:
- Exec summary (v1.2) is safe to share with no redactions; it contains high-level scope, methodology, and prioritized findings.
- For the sanitized findings we can provide: severity, affected surface (component names), brief impact description, and remediation status. We will redact PoC steps, specific exploit strings, and internal hostnames/IPs.

Remediation snapshot (for inclusion in the redaction log):
- RWD-2025-101 (High): SQLi in legacy analytics endpoint — remediated 2026-01-20; verified by retest.
- RWD-2025-118 (Medium): Insecure CORS on ingestion API — remediation in progress; patch ETA 2026-02-25.
- RWD-2025-127 (Low): Info leakage via debug header — configuration change pushed 2026-02-10.

Timing: once NDA markups are resolved, security can produce sanitized findings + redaction log within 3 business days and deliver the exec summary immediately. Full unredacted report requires an approved redaction list and a controlled access review (longer).

I'll attach the exec summary we usually share; redact flags are noted in the header.

-Rafael\Senior Security Engineer\Redwood Inference

Hi Jon/Ellie —

Thanks for the markups, Ellie. Rafael and I discussed and Redwood is comfortable with the sanitized sharing approach you outlined: we will provide the executive summary (attached) with no redactions, and a sanitized findings addendum that includes severity, affected component, impact summary, and remediation status. We will explicitly redact PoC details, exploit strings, and internal identifiers.

Next steps for speed:
- Ellie, please send your redlined NDA back to me (if possible by EOD today) and we will route to our legal for rapid approval.
- Rafael will prepare the sanitized findings + redaction log within 3 business days of NDA agreement.
- If you want, Rafael can join a 30-min call to walk through the findings after you review the exec summary.

Attaching: redwood_pen_test_exec_summary_v1.2.pdf and our NDA template (again).

Best,
Laura Bennett\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference
